items.title: Mr. and Mrs. A.C. Synigal Interview, 1962-05-24
items.q: He stopped with Miss Romania. That's my daughter's mother-in-law living in Algiers.

ctx.x: Oh, you didn't play it then, you just knew it. Oh, no, no, I was too young.

Oh. I was too young. But I played with him. I'll tell you how it was. We were here, as I told you, I was 14 years old when we moved here. And I married when I was 18. So, all the people in the country, we knew, we knew we, instead of sending them an invitation, my mother said, well, we'll make a trip, go out there and invite them. Invite them. So we were going all out in the country, it was different. And everyone was giving us a chicken, a hog, a pig, you know, all that. Oh, we needed, we had to create those…
I was thinking, trying to think about some of the people I know of from Donaldsonville. There was a guitar player named Joey Sales or something. But I guess he moved down here. Joey Sales?
